digest.headline: Technology stocks sold off globally as Japan reported a record currency intervention and Chinese banks raised dollar deposit rates.

lede.b: The Nasdaq stock index is a collection of shares from major technology companies. On Friday at 16:00, it suffered a record sell-off that hit artificial intelligence funds. A stock index tracks the overall value of a group of companies. Shares are small pieces of ownership in a business. Futures are contracts to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a future date. Investors pulled money out of technology stocks across the world. Gold prices climbed by over 1% while investors waited for inflation data. Inflation is the rate at which the cost of goods and services rises over time.
lede.i: The Nasdaq closed on Friday at 16:00 following a record sell-off that rattled artificial intelligence funds, while inflation data approached. Futures on the index remained jittery as equity markets experienced a risk-off shift. Global technology shares dropped, pulling the FTSE 100 down to 10,673.94 and weighing on German automakers. Sterling dipped against the US dollar as foreign exchange traders sought American currency during the broader sector rout.
lede.a: Midterm results triggered a record Nasdaq sell-off that rattled chip and artificial intelligence funds on Friday at 16:00. The risk-off transmission channel compressed valuations across European benchmarks, pulling the FTSE 100 to 10,673.94 and capping the DAX at 25,820.36 points. Sterling weakened against the greenback as liquidity flows favored safe-haven dollar assets during the technology-led unwinding.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Nasdaq sell-off and gold price movements

stories.t: Stock Indices Experience Pullback Following Midterm Results
stories.src: KuCoin · CNBC TV18 · The Daily Upside
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list of many tech company shares grouped together to track how the market is doing. It closed on Friday at 16:00 and saw jittery futures alongside a record sell-off triggered by midterm results. Shares in chip and artificial intelligence funds rattled as the S&P 500 index, another major basket of American company stocks, pulled back after the Stockholm Stock Exchange closed.
stories.i: The Nasdaq closed on Friday at 16:00 as midterm results triggered a record sell-off that rattled chip and artificial intelligence funds. Futures for the index remained jittery. The S&P 500 index subsequently pulled back after the Stockholm Stock Exchange closed.
stories.a: Midterm results precipitated a record sell-off across the Nasdaq, destabilising artificial intelligence and semiconductor allocations while leaving futures volatile. The S&P 500 mirrored this downward momentum, pulling back subsequent to the close of the Stockholm Stock Exchange.

stories.t: Gold Climbs Higher Ahead of Economic Data Releases
stories.b: Gold prices rallied more than 1% as investors awaited US inflation data. Inflation is the rising cost of everyday goods and services over time. State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust history suggests that the previous week's selloff functioned as a buying opportunity.
stories.i: Gold prices rallied by more than 1% as investors awaited incoming US inflation data. State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust history suggests that the preceding week's selloff represented a buying opportunity.
stories.a: Bullion rallied over 1% in anticipation of upcoming US inflation prints. Historical analogues cited by State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust indicate that the prior week's liquidation functioned as a tactical entry point.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: FTSE slips on AI rout and sterling dips

stories.t: FTSE 100 drops following global technology sell-off
stories.b: The FTSE 100 is a major stock index, which is a list tracking the overall value of the biggest companies traded in London. The FTSE 100 slipped to 10,673.94 points at the end of the week. Global technology shares fell during a wider market downturn. Investors responded to the technology rout by moving away from riskier assets.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index declined to 10,673.94 following a global technology sell-off. Equity markets experienced a risk-off shift as technology shares dropped. Investors pulled capital from risk assets in response to the broader sector rout.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 closed down at 10,673.94 amidst a global technology sector repricing. Broad-based equity liquidations reflected a risk-off regime driven by international artificial intelligence jitters. Cross-asset flows demonstrated capital flight from equities into safe havens.

stories.t: Sterling weakens against the dollar amid stock market decline
stories.b: Sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom, often referred to as the pound. The currency dipped in value against the US dollar. Stock market losses boosted demand for the dollar. Traders shifted capital toward American currency during the wider equity drop.
stories.i: Sterling dipped against the US dollar as a global stock market rout increased demand for American currency. Foreign exchange traders favored the dollar during the broader risk-off move. The currency decline accompanied the drop in equity benchmarks.
stories.a: Sterling depreciated against the US dollar as international equity liquidation spurred safe-haven demand for greenbacks. Foreign exchange desks recorded broad dollar outperformance during the risk-off session. The currency move tracked the wider contraction in risk appetite.

stories.t: DAX Reaches Record Before Flat Close
stories.b: The DAX index measures the value of big German companies. It ended flat at 25,820.36 points. This followed a record high and a sharp drop of 1.92% on Friday.
stories.i: The DAX index finished flat at 25,820.36 points. The session followed a record high and a 1.92% reversal on Friday.
stories.a: The DAX 40 settled at 25,820.36 points after mean-reverting from a record peak. Friday's 1.92% drawdown neutralized earlier intra-week gains, leaving the index flat on the weekly print.

stories.t: Technology Selloff Hits German Automakers
stories.b: Volkswagen shares dropped by 2.5% because of a wider chip rout. Meanwhile, BASF won awards for its automotive plastics. Tech-led selling weighed on share prices across the sector.
stories.i: Volkswagen shares dropped 2.5% amid a broader chip sector rout. BASF secured automotive plastics accolades while tech-led selling weighed on valuations.
stories.a: Volkswagen shares retreated 2.5% in response to semiconductor sector weakness. BASF garnered industry recognition for automotive plastics while broader tech-led liquidation compressed equity valuations.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Corporate acquisitions and record currency interventions in Japan

stories.t: Mitsui Chemicals and DBJ Agree to Purchase JSR
stories.b: Mitsui Chemicals and the Development Bank of Japan agreed to buy JSR for $11.6 billion. JSR is a company focused on electronics. The deal involves two major buyers joining forces. The transaction total reaches $11.6 billion.
stories.i: Mitsui Chemicals and the Development Bank of Japan announced a $11.6 billion acquisition of JSR. The transaction targets the electronics sector. Both buyers structured the buyout to consolidate technological assets.
stories.a: Mitsui Chemicals and the Development Bank of Japan agreed to acquire JSR for $11.6 billion. The transaction reflects consolidation within the electronics supply chain. The capital deployment hinges on long-term demand for specialized semiconductor materials.

stories.t: Japan Records Massive Currency Intervention in July
stories.src: The Economic Times · JIJI PRESS · NHKニュース
stories.b: Japan spent a record sum to buy its own money in July. The total reached 7.9 trillion yen, which equals $50 billion. Officials executed this massive intervention in a single day. The government stepped into the currency market to influence the exchange rate.
stories.i: Japan spent a record 7.9 trillion yen, or $50 billion, in a single day of forex intervention in July. The Ministry of Finance executed the massive currency defense operation on July 30. Authorities intervened directly in the market to counter depreciation pressures.
stories.a: Japan recorded a single-day forex intervention of 7.9 trillion yen, equivalent to $50 billion, on July 30. The unprecedented capital outlay underscores official determination to counter speculative short positions. The intervention scale exceeded prior historical benchmarks for single-session currency support.

politics.b: Government officials managed massive currency interventions. Leaders oversaw corporate acquisitions.
politics.i: Policymakers authorized record foreign exchange interventions totaling 7.9 trillion yen. State entities partnered in corporate buyouts.
politics.a: Fiscal authorities executed an unprecedented 7.9 trillion yen single-day currency intervention in July. State-backed financial institutions participated in major industrial consolidation deals.

China.label: China
China.sub: Chinese banks boost dollar deposit rates to cool yuan

stories.t: Chinese Banks Raise US Dollar Deposit Rates
stories.b: Chinese banks lifted the interest rates they pay on US dollar deposits. This move aims to slow down the rapid rise of the Chinese currency, known as the yuan. When banks pay more for dollar deposits, people want to hold more dollars instead of yuan. That extra demand helps cool down the strong yuan. Beijing sought this change to smooth out currency movements.
stories.i: Chinese banks raised US dollar deposit rates to temper the appreciating yuan. Higher yields on dollar holdings alter the return profile for corporate treasurers. This adjustment discourages aggressive selling of the greenback. Beijing deployed this measure to smooth out cross-border currency momentum.
stories.a: State-backed financial institutions increased US dollar deposit rates to counter relentless yuan appreciation pressure. The policy tweak alters domestic FX conversion incentives by enhancing greenback retention appeal. This administrative intervention aims to stem unilateral momentum without direct spot market intervention.

stories.t: Zhuhai State-Owned Platforms Accelerate Asset Shuffle
stories.b: Gree Group took over the Huafa Marriott Hotel for about 2 billion yuan. This deal is part of a broader asset shuffle by state-owned platforms in Zhuhai. Companies in the region are rearranging their property holdings. The transaction shows large local corporate restructuring.
stories.i: Gree Group acquired the Huafa Marriott Hotel for approximately 2 billion yuan. Zhuhai state-owned platforms accelerated their ongoing asset shuffle through this transaction. Local entities continue restructuring regional hospitality and corporate holdings. This deal highlights active portfolio adjustments among municipal operators.
stories.a: Gree Group executed a 2 billion yuan takeover of the Huafa Marriott Hotel. The transaction underscores accelerated asset shuffling among Zhuhai state-owned platforms. Municipal balance sheet optimization drives these intra-state corporate reallocations. Local asset consolidation remains a dominant theme across regional industrial portfolios.

politics.b: Beijing authorities directed banks to adjust deposit rates to manage the national currency.
politics.i: Regulators orchestrated monetary adjustments via state-run banks to curb currency appreciation.
politics.a: State guidance directed commercial lenders to recalibrate deposit rates as an FX management tool.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI money market data and Nifty 50 stock index movements

stories.t: Nifty 50 achieves weekly gains amid broader market movements
stories.b: The Nifty 50 is a stock index, which is a group of shares tracking the performance of major companies. This stock group posted an 8.6% weekly gain. A global sell-off helped drive this strong performance. Trading for the Sensex and Nifty began in the red on November 9, 2026. This means the indexes opened lower than their previous close.
stories.i: The Nifty 50 index recorded an 8.6% weekly gain driven by a global sell-off. Market participants observed the Sensex and Nifty beginning trading in the red on November 9, 2026. GIFT Nifty pointed to a firm open with a 55-point rise earlier. Analysts at CLSA projected a long-term Nifty target of 40,000.
stories.a: The Nifty 50 printed an 8.6% weekly gain amid a global sell-off before opening in the red on November 9, 2026. GIFT Nifty futures implied a 55-point higher open. Meanwhile, CLSA strategist Laurence Balanco highlighted a long-term Nifty target of 40,000 alongside a 20% upside projection for banking stocks.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India executes variable rate repo auction
stories.b: The central bank manages the supply of money in the economy. This central bank held a 4-day variable rate repo auction on November 9, 2026. Lenders asked for 62,872 crore rupees in total bids. The institution notified an amount of 50,000 crore rupees. It ultimately allotted 50,003 crore rupees at a weighted average rate of 5.54%.
stories.i: The central bank conducted a 4-day variable rate repo auction on November 9, 2026, receiving 62,872 crore rupees in bids against a notified amount of 50,000 crore rupees. Authorities allotted 50,003 crore rupees with a cut-off rate of 5.51%. The weighted average rate settled at 5.54% with a partial allotment percentage of 15.18% at the cut-off rate.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India allotted 50,003 crore rupees through its 4-day variable rate repo auction on November 9, 2026. Aggregate bids reached 62,872 crore rupees against the 50,000 crore rupee notified amount. The operation printed a 5.51% cut-off rate and a 5.54% weighted average rate, with bids at the cut-off receiving a 15.18% partial allotment.

politics.b: Axis Mutual Fund discussed US midterm election results. The firm stated these results could boost foreign portfolio investments into India. Officials noted this might ease pressure on the rupee.
politics.i: Axis Mutual Fund noted that US midterm election results could influence foreign portfolio investor inflows. Market participants evaluated how these political outcomes might ease currency pressure on the rupee.
politics.a: Axis MF assessed that US midterm results could catalyze foreign portfolio investment inflows into India. Analysts linked this potential shift to mitigating depreciation pressure on the rupee.

stories.t: Petrobras advances field projects and credit standing
stories.b: Petrobras secured approval for a floating production storage and offloading vessel concept at the Tupi Field. The company received a credit profile upgrade for its standalone operations. Petrobras also started using the Cardano blockchain to track sustainable aviation fuel.
stories.i: Petrobras advanced the Tupi Field redevelopment with LR approval for an FPSO concept. The state-controlled energy producer also secured a standalone credit profile upgrade. Operations expanded further as Petrobras began using the Cardano blockchain to track sustainable aviation fuel.
stories.a: Petrobras progressed its Tupi Field redevelopment following LR approval for its FPSO concept. Standalone credit metrics improved as the entity secured an agency upgrade. Concurrently, the firm integrated the Cardano blockchain for transparent tracking of sustainable aviation fuel.

stories.t: Contract wins and stakeholder adjustments around Petrobras
stories.b: Rina won a subsea decommissioning contract from Petrobras. Point Nemo Capital cut its stake in Petrobras stock. Karoon Energy faced an extended 12% export tax in Brazil.
stories.i: Rina secured a subsea decommissioning contract from Petrobras. Point Nemo Capital reduced its shareholding stake in the Brazilian oil producer. Meanwhile, Karoon Energy continued to face an extended 12% export tax in Brazil.
stories.a: Rina secured a subsea decommissioning award from Petrobras. Institutional positioning shifted as Point Nemo Capital trimmed its equity stake in the issuer. Externally, Karoon Energy managed the persistence of Brazil's extended 12% export tax.

politics.b: Government policies and tax rules affect energy firms operating in Brazil. State-controlled entities manage large infrastructure assets and development projects. Export levies impact foreign energy companies working in the region.
politics.i: State involvement shapes the operational environment for major energy producers in Brazil. Regulatory frameworks dictate export levies, such as the 12% tax affecting external operators. Corporate governance and state planning steer large-scale offshore field developments.
politics.a: State influence permeates the Brazilian energy sector through majority equity stakes and regulatory oversight. Fiscal policy tools, including the extended 12% export tax, directly alter cash flow dynamics for foreign producers. Strategic capital allocation by state enterprises anchors domestic infrastructure and redevelopment pipelines.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia

stories.t: Houthi Attack Damages Aramco Tower in Riyadh
stories.b: A missile strike hit a large corporate tower in the capital city of Riyadh. The building belongs to Saudi Aramco, a massive state-run oil company. Debris from the incoming projectiles caused damage across nine floors of the structure located inside a major financial district. Saudi forces intercepted incoming missiles during the aerial assault.
stories.i: A missile strike damaged a prominent tower belonging to Saudi Aramco within the financial district of Riyadh. Incoming projectiles damaged nine floors of the high-rise structure after missile debris scattered across the commercial hub. Saudi defense systems intercepted the incoming attack launched by Houthi forces.
stories.a: A targeted Houthi aerial assault breached defenses to damage nine floors of the iconic Saudi Aramco tower in the capital's central financial district. Interception debris compounded structural impacts across the high-rise commercial asset. The incident marks a rare physical strike directly hitting core financial and corporate infrastructure in Riyadh.

stories.t: Retaliatory Operations and Regional Security Updates
stories.src: The Business Standard · The National · IndiaIPO
stories.b: A military operation in Yemen followed the strike in Riyadh and left 72 people dead. Meanwhile, political figures in the United States played down the likelihood of new military actions against Iran. Global commodity markets tracked oil pricing as Brent crude hovered near $97 per barrel.
stories.i: A retaliatory military operation in Yemen caused 72 deaths in the wake of the capital city attack. In international diplomacy, United States officials downplayed the prospect of imminent strikes targeting Iran. Energy markets monitored crude benchmarks closely as Brent traded around $97 per barrel.
stories.a: A lethal retaliatory operation in Yemen resulted in 72 fatalities following the domestic security breach. Concurrently, external diplomatic statements minimized expectations of near-term escalation against Iran. Energy benchmarks responded cautiously, with Brent crude settling near $97 per barrel.

politics.b: Regional conflicts intensified as missile attacks struck the capital of Saudi Arabia. Security forces intercepted multiple airborne threats while military operations in Yemen followed the incident. International leaders commented on broader Middle Eastern security and potential actions involving Iran.
politics.i: Geopolitical tensions escalated sharply after cross-border missile strikes damaged infrastructure in Riyadh. Interception systems neutralized incoming threats while retaliatory operations in Yemen caused multiple casualties. Global powers continued calibrating their diplomatic stances regarding regional adversaries.
politics.a: Cross-border kinetic strikes penetrating Riyadh airspace triggered active air defense responses and subsequent regional military retaliation. The physical damage to critical commercial infrastructure in the financial district heightened operational risk premiums across the peninsula. Diplomatic signalling from international allies meanwhile sought to temper expectations of broader regional escalation.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira movements and stock market drops in Nigeria

stories.t: Exchange Rate Shifts as Dollar Demand Rises
stories.src: The Guardian Nigeria News · MarketForces Africa
stories.b: The national money of Nigeria is the naira. When people want to buy foreign money like the dollar, the price can move up and down. The naira weakened by 1.79% to reach N1,394 per dollar. This happened because more people wanted to buy foreign cash.
stories.i: The naira weakened by 1.79% to trade at N1,394 per dollar. Higher foreign exchange demand drove the currency down in the market. Tighter dollar supply across official channels pressured the local unit further.
stories.a: The spot rate for the naira depreciated by 1.79% to N1,394 per dollar. Amplified foreign exchange demand outpaced available liquidity. Constrained dollar availability in the official window continued to drive downward pressure on the currency.

stories.t: Nigerian Exchange Loses Value Amid Equity Sell-Off
stories.b: Shares are tiny pieces of ownership in a business. Companies listed on the stock exchange saw their total worth drop by N3.52 trillion. Investors sold off large stakes in major corporations, causing this major fall in total value.
stories.i: Equities on the Nigerian Exchange dropped by N3.52 trillion in total value. A widespread sell-off of blue-chip stocks drove the market down. Major corporate shares faced intense liquidation from investors.
stories.a: Market capitalization on the Nigerian Exchange contracted by N3.52 trillion. Heavy institutional distribution in blue-chip equities precipitated the broader market decline. Asset managers rebalanced portfolios away from large-cap counters amid persistent macro headwinds.

politics.b: Political critics argued about who should take credit for the currency's recent recovery. Groups told leaders to stop blaming others for economic hardships.
politics.i: Opposition voices disputed government claims regarding currency recovery. Critics urged officials to accept responsibility for ongoing economic hardships.

stories.b: Miners are companies that dig valuable metals out of the ground. They helped Australian shares recover from a morning drop. The rest of the market stayed quiet while mining firms did the heavy lifting. Mining shares finished the session with strong gains.
stories.i: Mining companies drove a recovery in Australian equities after an early session decline. Broader market sectors remained sluggish throughout the trading day. The resources sector offset weakness across the rest of the index.
stories.a: Resource-heavy sectors catalyzed a intraday reversal on the local bourse, neutralizing early macro headwinds. Broader index constituents failed to generate meaningful participation. Sector concentration dominated index performance.
